title: Hvar Prices & Budget for 2027: Real Daily Costs
metaDescription: Hvar 2027 budget guide: ferry, hotel, food and beach club prices in euros, how costs have risen, and daily budgets from €90 to €400+ per person.
content:
## How Much Does Hvar Cost in 2027?

Hvar is one of the most expensive islands in Croatia, and the gap between Hvar Town and the rest of the island is large. Hvar Town in July and August combines a superyacht harbour, beach clubs and a nightlife scene, and prices follow. Stari Grad, Jelsa and the south-coast villages cost noticeably less.

No official 2027 price lists exist yet. The figures below take the 2026 price level and add a realistic 3–6% rise for 2027, in line with continued tourism demand and euro-era inflation in Croatia. Treat them as planning ranges, not quotes.

### Daily budget per person, 2027 estimate

| Travel style | Per person per day (excluding flights) | What it covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Budget | €90–130 | Hostel or shared apartment, bakery and market food, one konoba dinner, free beaches, car ferry |
| Mid-range | €180–280 | Double room split between two, catamaran, two restaurant meals, one boat trip, a few drinks |
| Luxury | €400+ | Five-star hotel, beach club days, fine dining, private boat or speedboat |

A 2026 benchmark for context: a typical traveller spent roughly €130 a day. Mid-range travellers commonly reported €150–250. A week in Hvar averaged about €900 per person on the lower end. Adding 2027 increases puts a realistic one-week mid-range trip for one person at about €1,300–1,800, with accommodation shared between two.

## How Have Hvar Prices Changed Recently?

Three changes stand out compared with a few years ago.

- **Accommodation moved up the most.** A 3-star hotel in Hvar Town now averages about €105 a night across the year, a 4-star about €170, and a 5-star about €430. In August, luxury rooms run €250–435.
- **Restaurant prices converged on tourist-city levels.** Mains on the waterfront cost €18–25, against €12–18 on less-visited islands. Beach club cocktails reach €12–15, against €8–10 elsewhere.
- **Ferry fares stayed relatively stable.** The Jadrolinija catamaran fare from Split to Hvar Town sits at €25 in high season. Cheaper routes exist, but the headline fare has barely moved.

The pattern for 2027 is the same: the biggest increases hit rooms and drinks, and transport rises least.

## Getting to Hvar: Ferry and Catamaran Costs

### Catamaran to Hvar Town

The direct Jadrolinija catamaran (line 641) from Split to Hvar Town takes about 1 hour and costs about €25 one way. In 2026 it ran from mid-May to mid-October, with departures from Split around 10:10 and 16:00 in high season. Return departures from Hvar left around 11:30 and 17:25. The fare is identical in both directions. Krilo (Kapetan Luka) and TP Line also operate, and Krilo's slower route via Milna on Brač starts around €15.

Children under 12 pay half price and under-3s travel free. Large luggage costs about €5 extra per piece. In July and August there are up to 19 sailings a day, but weekend departures can sell out one to two weeks ahead.

### Car ferry to Stari Grad

The Jadrolinija car ferry (line 635) runs from Split to Stari Grad in about 1 hour 50 minutes. A foot passenger pays €8.40 in peak season, or €5.90 off-season. A car costs about €47.60 in peak season. Stari Grad is on the opposite end of the island from Hvar Town, about 20 km away. Check which port suits your accommodation before booking.

**Local tip:** Buy catamaran tickets online. The small ticket window at Hvar's port has queues in summer and a cash-only reputation.

## Accommodation Prices in Hvar

- **Hostel dorm bed:** €25–35 a night in shoulder season, higher in July and August.
- **Mid-range hotel or apartment:** €80–150 in shoulder season. Peak weeks in Hvar Town move this to roughly €120–180 for 2027.
- **Four-star hotels:** Around €170–230. Pharos Hvar Bayhill Hotel and Podstine Hotel sit in this tier, with late-August rates of about €190–250 for a double.
- **Luxury:** Adriana Hvar Spa Hotel runs about €310 in summer, and Amfora Hvar Grand Beach Resort €390–435. Palace Elisabeth starts above €300 in peak season.

Book 2027 summer rooms in Hvar Town by early spring. Stari Grad and Jelsa apartments are often 25–40% cheaper than comparable rooms in Hvar Town, and both are connected by bus or short taxi rides.

## Food and Drink Prices

- **Bakery breakfast and coffee:** €4–8.
- **Cheap meal (konoba, pizza, grill):** €13–18.
- **Waterfront main course in Hvar Town:** €18–25. Add €32 or more for a typical dinner with a drink.
- **Fish by weight:** Usually the most expensive line on any menu. Ask the weight and price per kilo before ordering.
- **Beach club cocktail:** €12–15, with nightlife venues at €14–20.
- **Supermarket picnic:** €6–10 per person.

The fastest way to cut costs is to eat the main meal away from the main square. Streets behind the harbour and villages such as Stari Grad and Jelsa offer similar Dalmatian dishes for €12–18 a main.

## Beach Clubs and Pakleni Islands

The Pakleni Islands sit just offshore from Hvar Town. A taxi boat to Palmižana costs about €8 each way, and a loungers-and-umbrella set at a beach club runs about €15–35 at modest venues. Famous venues near town, including Hula Hula and the Carpe Diem Beach area, charge €50 or more for premium sunbeds. A group boat trip to several coves typically costs €40–70 per person.

Public beaches are free. Arrive early and bring your own umbrella.

The cheaper option wins here. A beach club day costing €50 and up looks appealing on social media. In practice, a €16 return taxi boat, a rented umbrella and lunch on Palmižana gives the same swim and the same view for under €60 total, compared with €100+ at the high-profile venues.

## Getting Around the Island

Public transport is limited, with a few daily buses linking Hvar Town, Stari Grad and Jelsa. Taxis charge about €1.40 per km on the standard tariff, so crossing the island by taxi adds up quickly. A scooter costs roughly €30–35 a day and is the cheapest way to reach south-coast villages. Car rental is practical only if you bring a vehicle on the car ferry or stay outside Hvar Town.

## Sample 2027 Budgets

### Three days, mid-range, per person

- Return catamaran: about €50–54
- Three nights at a shared room: €150–250 (your share)
- Meals: €60–90 a day
- Pakleni Islands day with taxi boat and lounger: about €30–45
- Drinks and extras: €40–80
- **Total:** roughly €650–900

### One week, budget, per person

- Car ferry return: about €17–20
- Seven nights in a hostel or shared apartment: €200–300
- Food (markets, bakeries, one meal out each day): €250–350
- Scooter or boat extras: €60–120
- **Total:** roughly €600–800 for off-peak weeks, nearer €900 in August

## When to Go to Keep Costs Down

June and September are the best value. The sea is warm, catamarans run frequently, and room rates fall below August levels by 30% or more. May and early October save more but have reduced ferry schedules. August carries the highest hotel rates, difficult dinner reservations after 20:00 and sold-out catamarans.

## Money-Saving Tips

- Base yourself in Stari Grad or Jelsa and take the bus into Hvar Town.
- Use the cheaper Krilo route via Milna if you are not in a hurry.
- Choose the car ferry to Stari Grad as a foot passenger at €8.40.
- Pay for a beach club only on days when you want one.
- Fill a water bottle from the tap. Croatian tap water is drinkable.
- Check the daily menu on boards before sitting down, and avoid tables without printed prices.

faq.question: How much does a trip to Hvar cost per day in 2027?
faq.answer: Expect about €90–130 per person on a budget, €180–280 mid-range and €400+ for luxury. These estimates add 3–6% to 2026 prices, and July and August sit at the top of each range.

faq.question: Is Hvar expensive compared to other Croatian islands?
faq.answer: Yes. Hvar Town restaurant mains cost €18–25 versus €12–18 on quieter islands, and cocktails run €12–15 against €8–10. Stari Grad and Jelsa are significantly cheaper than Hvar Town.

faq.question: How much is the ferry from Split to Hvar?
faq.answer: The direct Jadrolinija catamaran to Hvar Town costs about €23–25 one way and takes roughly 1 hour. The car ferry to Stari Grad costs €8.40 for a foot passenger in peak season and takes about 1 hour 50 minutes.

faq.question: How much does a hotel in Hvar cost per night?
faq.answer: Hostel beds cost €25–35, mid-range rooms €80–150 in shoulder season, 4-star hotels around €170–230, and 5-star properties €300–435 in summer. Peak-season mid-range rooms in Hvar Town typically start at €120–180.

faq.question: What is the cheapest month to visit Hvar?
faq.answer: May, early June, September and early October have the lowest accommodation prices. June and September offer the best balance of warm sea, full ferry schedules and rates well below August.

faq.question: Do I need to book Hvar ferries in advance?
faq.answer: In July and August, yes. Catamarans on weekends can sell out one to two weeks ahead. Foot passengers on the car ferry to Stari Grad can usually buy tickets on the day, but vehicles should be booked ahead.

faq.question: Are the beaches in Hvar free?
faq.answer: Public beaches in Hvar Town, the Pakleni Islands and the south coast are free. Beach clubs charge €15–35 at modest venues and €50 or more at popular ones for sunbeds and service.

quickAnswer: Plan on about €90–130 per person per day on a budget in Hvar in 2027, €180–280 mid-range, and €400+ for luxury. These figures extend 2026 prices by roughly 3–6%. The catamaran from Split is about €25 one way, and mid-range rooms in July and August start around €120–180 a night.
